stop_status: CLEAR after repair. STOP was invoked on three confirmed memory-safety defects: B16-D2 (heap-use-after-free in SSL_set_srp_server_param when the caller passes the pointer SSL_get_srp_userinfo returned), B16-D3 (NULL dereference/abort in ENGINE_unregister_pkey_asn1_meths(NULL)), and B16-D1 (a refused structural reference returned a borrowed EVP_PKEY_ASN1_METHOD pointer while owning no engine reference). A fourth ownership defect (B16-D4, displaced ephemeral key not released) and a fifth concurrency defect (B16-D5, unsynchronised initialized_engines stack allowing a finish-vs-init heap-use-after-free and a lost stack) were repaired as well. D2 and D3 have observed pre-fix negative controls (ASan heap-use-after-free; SIGABRT null dereference); D1 has an observed pre-fix assertion failure (borrowed method returned). D5's race cannot be forced deterministically without a scheduling hook: its first-class canary is NOT_RUN and a serialised regression test passes after the repair. No unresolved STOP condition remains. No safe caller can cause UB through the audited interfaces under the stated contracts; hidden obligations are 0. Nothing is promoted to SAFETY_DISCHARGED.

authority.source: openssl-3.6.4 ssl/tls_srp.c :33-545, ssl/statem/extensions_clnt.c :16-878 (client constructors), crypto/engine/eng_cnf.c :19-184, crypto/engine/tb_asnmth.c :26-221. The four authority files were fetched for this audit; the crate's own line/site annotations were checked against them.
authority.abi: C ABI unchanged: no exported symbol, signature, #[repr(C)] layout, allocator-seam coordinate or unsafe lint attribute changed. The two new test modules are #[cfg(test)] only.
external_contracts: SrpCtx is a plain #[repr(C)] credential block on SslCtx/Ssl: login/info are NULL or CRYPTO_strdup blocks owned by the block, and n/g/s/b_pub/a_pub/a/b/v are NULL or owned BIGNUMs. srp_ctx_free is the block's single release.
SSL_set_srp_server_param takes a borrowed info string and copies it with CRYPTO_strdup; the argument may alias the connection's current field (e.g. the pointer SSL_get_srp_userinfo returned).
The SRP callbacks (username/verify/password) are application-controlled; the username callback is invoked with the live SSL and a writable alert slot and must not free the connection.

tls_construct_extensions/tls_construct_ctos_* own only their WPACKET writes and, for key_share, the generated EVP_PKEY they transfer to s3.tmp.pkey. The connection's ctx is live for every Ssl constructed by SSL_new.

CONF module init/finish callbacks may be invoked concurrently by CONF_modules_load (on different CONF objects) and by CONF_modules_unload. initialized_engines is a module-global stack; the engine init/finish hooks are application-controlled and must not run under the stack lock.

ENGINE.cmd_defns and the pkey_asn1_meths callback are caller-owned. The callback fills nids and/or the method slot; the returned EVP_PKEY_ASN1_METHOD belongs to the engine and is valid only while the caller holds an ENGINE reference.

ENGINE_pkey_asn1_find_str walks the table under the global engine read lock, as the authority does; the pkey_asn1_meths callback therefore runs under that read lock and must not request the engine write lock. On a refused structural up-ref the authority unlocks, raises ERR_R_CRYPTO_LIB and returns NULL without writing *pe.

boundaries.mechanism: credential-block ownership: srp_ctx_free, ctx/connection free and init internals
boundaries.contract: A live SrpCtx owns login/info (CRYPTO_strdup) and eight BIGNUMs exactly once; srp_ctx_free releases each through the seam at the authority's coordinates, zeroes the block and restores strength = SRP_MINIMAL_N. ssl_srp_ctx_init_intern zeroes the destination before any partial copy, duplicates only non-NULL sources, and on any failure releases exactly the fields acquired so far; ssl_ctx_srp_ctx_init_intern zeroes a fresh or caller-reset context.

boundaries.mechanism: server parameter setters and accessors: SSL_set_srp_server_param[_pw], SSL_get_srp_*
boundaries.contract: Password-string assignment duplicates before releasing the previous value, so an argument aliasing the current field is safe; every failed duplicate leaves the field NULL with the old block released, matching the authority's end state. BN fields are copied in place or duplicated; the accessors return borrowed pointers owned by the connection or context.

boundaries.mechanism: server-parameter callback edge and client A computation: srp_server_param_with_username, srp_password_from_info_cb, srp_calc_a_param
boundaries.contract: The username callback runs with no crate lock, no Rust reference held across it and the connection live; its alert output is a writable int. The random buffer is stack-local and cleansed on both success paths. The password callback duplicates a NULL-tolerant field through CRYPTO_strdup.

Each installer forwards to the established ssl3_ctx_ctrl/SSL_CTX_callback_ctrl arm. The callback pointer is stored as pointer bits and re-transmuted to its real type by the arm; it is never called through the placeholder signature.

boundaries.mechanism: framework and simple ClientHello constructors: tls_construct_extensions and the server_name/alpn/versions/psk_modes/RI/ec_formats/sig_algs/groups/etm/ems/ticket/pha builders
boundaries.contract: Every builder writes only through the live WPACKET and returns EXT_RETURN_FAIL without committing partial state (the caller abandons the packet). Member-buffer reads (hostname, ALPN, session ticket) come from owner-derived accessors that preserve the (ptr,len) invariant; the ticket read is NULL-checked and length-guarded.

The generated EVP_PKEY is transferred to s3.tmp.pkey only on EXT_RETURN_SENT and released on every failure; the encoded public key is released once through CRYPTO_free; the previous slot value is released before being displaced. The context dereferenced for libctx/propq is live for every SSL_new connection.

No application callback is invoked anywhere in this file; the only external operations are WPACKET writes and EVP key generation through the provider, with no crate lock held across them. Failure paths return the authority's EXT_RETURN_FAIL and leave no owned pointer live.

boundaries.mechanism: module stack ownership: INITIALIZED_ENGINES, int_engine_init, int_engine_module_finish
boundaries.contract: The stack pointer is published and mutated only under INITIALIZED_ENGINES_LOCK. int_engine_init takes the functional reference before the lock and records it under the lock; failure finishes the engine after dropping the lock. The finish walk pops one engine under the lock, finishes it with no lock held, and frees/clears the empty stack under the lock. No ENGINE callback or application code runs under the lock (lock order: none -> INITIALIZED_ENGINES_LOCK).

boundaries.mechanism: configuration walk and ctrl callback edge: int_engine_configure, int_engine_module_init
boundaries.contract: The CONF section stack is read for its call lifetime. ENGINE_by_id/ENGINE_ctrl_cmd_string/ENGINE_set_default_string/ENGINE_init are called with no eng_cnf lock held, so an application ctrl/init hook may re-enter configuration loading without deadlock; the structural ENGINE reference is released on every path.
The two 'static extern "C" callbacks and the static module name are published once through CONF_module_add under guard_ffi; no caller data is retained.

Registration forwards the callback's borrowed nids array to the engine table; the table stores a borrowed ENGINE owned by the global engine list. Unregistration of a live engine removes every occurrence under the engine write lock. A NULL argument is a documented no-op and never reaches the pile callback (which would dereference a NULL cached default).

boundaries.mechanism: by-name lookup and refcount transfer: ENGINE_get_pkey_asn1_meth[_str], ENGINE_pkey_asn1_find_str, look_str_cb
boundaries.contract: The string walk calls the application callback under the global engine read lock (authority order) and returns engine-owned method pointers. A match takes exactly one structural reference before returning the method; a refused checked increment unlocks, raises TB_ASNMTH_213 (ERR_R_CRYPTO_LIB) and returns NULL without writing *pe, so no caller receives a method without an engine reference.

boundaries.mechanism: method release at engine destruction: engine_pkey_asn1_meths_free
boundaries.contract: For each nid reported by the engine's callback, the method the callback hands back is released exactly once with EVP_PKEY_asn1_free. A NULL engine, a missing callback and a refused method are no-ops. The callback's nids array remains engine-owned and is not released.

defects.class: refcount refusal returned a borrowed method pointer with no engine reference (latent use-after-free)
defects.description: On a refused structural up-ref the pre-fix code set fstr.e = NULL and still fell through to return fstr.ameth. The caller therefore received an EVP_PKEY_ASN1_METHOD owned by an engine it held no reference to, while *pe was written NULL. The authority instead unlocks, raises ERR_R_CRYPTO_LIB (the generated TB_ASNMTH_213 site was present but unused) and returns NULL without touching *pe. The repair follows the authority exactly.
defects.control: engine::tb_asnmth::tests::a_refused_structural_reference_returns_no_method. Pre-fix: assertion `ameth.is_null()` failed (the borrowed method was returned). Post-fix: passes; *pe remains the caller's sentinel.

defects.class: heap-use-after-free read on a C-valid aliasing argument
defects.description: SSL_set_srp_server_param released the connection's old info string and then called CRYPTO_strdup(info). When a caller passes the pointer SSL_get_srp_userinfo(s) returned, info is the block just freed; the duplicate read freed memory (strlen/memcpy). The authority has the same order. The repair duplicates first, then releases the old block and assigns the duplicate, preserving the authority's end state on allocation failure.
defects.control: ssl::tls_srp::tests::server_param_accepts_its_own_userinfo_as_the_new_info under the dedicated ASan venue. Pre-fix: AddressSanitizer heap-use-after-free in runtime::mem::strlen (mem.rs:1019) reached from CRYPTO_strdup in tls_srp. Post-fix: 1 passed, 0 failed, no sanitizer report (ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=0; see escalation E1 for the unrelated leak).

defects.class: NULL dereference/abort on the function's own documented NULL-tolerant call
defects.description: ENGINE_unregister_pkey_asn1_meths forwarded a NULL engine to engine_table_unregister. int_unregister_cb compares the argument with each pile's cached default; on a pile whose funct is NULL (a non-defaulted registration) the comparison succeeds and engine_unlocked_finish(NULL) dereferences the NULL engine. The repair refuses NULL before entering the table walk; a NULL cannot name a registered engine.
defects.control: engine::tb_asnmth::tests::unregister_with_null_is_refused_before_the_pile_walk. Pre-fix: process abort with `null pointer dereference occurred` at eng_init.rs:91 (SIGABRT). Post-fix: passes.

defects.class: owned field overwritten without release (leak; no UB)
defects.description: tls_construct_ctos_key_share assigned the fresh EVP_PKEY to s3.tmp.pkey unconditionally. The slot owns the previous ephemeral, and a second construction (a retry or a future HRR path) would drop it without release. The authority's share-table arm reuses ks_pkey[0]; this reduced client has no table, so it now releases the displaced key before storing the new one, matching the established sibling pattern in statem_clnt.rs/statem_srvr.rs.
defects.control: Static ownership review plus the existing library tests; no wire-visible change and no focused canary (the pre-fix path is a leak, not UB, and is unreachable in the non-HRR stratum). NOT_RUN as a sanitizer canary.

defects.class: unsynchronised module-global stack: finish-vs-init heap-use-after-free and init-vs-init lost stack
defects.description: The authority uses a plain static with no lock. The crate's CONF registry documents that CONF_modules_load may run concurrently on different CONF objects, so two int_engine_init calls could both observe NULL and one could overwrite the other's freshly allocated stack (leaking the stack and the engines it records), and int_engine_module_finish could free the stack while a concurrent init pushed into it. The repair serialises only the stack allocation/push/pop/free under a module-local Mutex; ENGINE_init/ENGINE_finish (application hooks) run outside it, so callback reentrancy is preserved.
defects.control: engine::eng_cnf::tests::concurrent_init_records_every_engine_and_finish_releases_them passes after the repair. The race window it covers is scheduler-dependent, so a pre-fix deterministic canary is NOT_RUN (no scheduling hook); the post-fix test asserts both functional references are recorded and both released.

sweep.result: Every SrpCtx field was traced through init, copy, failure and release. The one aliasing UAF (B16-D2) is repaired; all failure paths release only fields acquired so far. Repeated init/setter calls reproduce the authority's own leaks (B16-R1/R2), recorded rather than silently fixed.

The username/password callbacks are invoked with no crate lock and no Rust reference held across them; the connection is live per the C contract. A callback that frees the connection remains outside that contract (authority contract).

sweep.concern: Client extension construction and packet ownership
sweep.result: Every builder was compared with the fetched authority constructors. WPACKET sequences, guards and EXT_RETURN values match for the landed rows. The only owned slot transferred is s3.tmp.pkey, and its displaced value is now released (B16-D4). No callback runs in this file.

sweep.concern: ENGINE configuration module stack and callbacks
sweep.result: The stack's publication, push, pop, free and clear are all under one module-local lock; ENGINE callbacks and ctrl/init hooks run outside it. The CONF walk itself remains the authority's: a callback that mutates the section being walked is outside the C contract (B16-R7).

sweep.concern: ASN.1 method table lookup, refcount and callbacks
sweep.result: Every registration/unregistration/select path was checked against tb_asnmth.c and eng_table.c. The by-name walk holds the read lock across the application callback (authority order; B16-R5), takes exactly one structural reference on a match, and now fails closed on a refused increment (B16-D1). NULL unregistration is refused before the pile walk (B16-D3).

compatibility.tls_srp: B16-D2 changes only the order of two operations: for a non-aliasing argument the observable result and the allocation-failure end state are identical; for an aliasing argument the authority reads freed memory and this crate now succeeds. The authority's error-queue raises on BN/strdup failure remain unimplemented (B16-R4, pre-existing). The init-failure strength value differs (B16-R3, unobservable on SSL_new's failure path).
compatibility.extensions_clnt: B16-D4 releases a displaced key; the wire bytes and EXT_RETURN values are unchanged. The reduced client still regenerates rather than reusing ks_pkey[0] in an HRR path, which is the pre-existing recorded boundary (the stratum is non-HRR).
compatibility.eng_cnf: B16-D5 serialises access to the stack without changing the config walk, the pop order, the callback order or the error sites. Concurrent loads no longer lose an engine record; sequential authority behaviour is unchanged.
compatibility.tb_asnmth: B16-D3 turns an authority-parity crash into a no-op for a NULL unregistration. B16-D1 matches the authority's refusal answer exactly (NULL method, *pe untouched, TB_ASNMTH_213). Valid-engine paths are unchanged. The wrong 'NULL is allowed' contracts on the register/get/set functions were corrected to non-NULL.
compatibility.authority_differential: NOT_RUN for B16-D1/D2/D3/D5. The authority reads freed memory for B16-D2 and aborts for B16-D3, so a differential would be a crash comparison rather than an output comparison; B16-D1's refusal requires an artificial saturated count on both sides. The existing library suite was run unchanged.

miri.blocker: the court's product toolchain is 1.98.1-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu without the miri component; the dedicated ASan venue covered the B16-D2 UAF control instead.

loom_or_tsan: NOT_RUN. The B16-D5 repair is a serialisation argument plus a threaded regression test; no Loom or TSan model was invoked, and no deterministic pre-fix schedule was constructed.
new_unsafe_assumptions_note: No new abstraction or caller obligation. The tb_asnmth refusal branch adds the unlock and raise that the authority performs; the eng_cnf lock adds no unsafe operation. The remaining C-ABI obligations (the pkey_asn1_meths callback runs under the engine read lock; CONF callbacks must not mutate the section being walked; SRP callbacks must not free the connection) are stated in the boundary contracts above, so they are retained and visible, not hidden.
unsafe_operations_introduced_detail: Two new production unsafe blocks in ENGINE_pkey_asn1_find_str's refusal arm: CRYPTO_THREAD_unlock(global_engine_lock()) and raise_site(&TB_ASNMTH_213), both under explicit SAFETY comments. The other repairs add no unsafe expression: the tls_srp reorder reuses its existing block, the extensions_clnt release is one FFI call inside the existing block, and the eng_cnf lock is safe Rust.
safe_callers_can_cause_ub_note: Under the stated contracts, no safe Rust caller can cause UB through these boundaries. The audited entry points are C ABI functions whose pointer/lifetime preconditions are documented at each site; within those contracts the repaired paths release or refuse exactly as stated. The application callbacks remain C contracts, not hidden Rust obligations.

escalations.description: The ASan venue additionally reported an 84-byte direct leak allocated by raise_site_dynamic_data (runtime/err.rs:1012) through EVP_MD_fetch during SSL_CTX_new_ex. It is unrelated to the B16 files and does not affect the UAF result, but it should be assigned to the ERR/EVP or SSL_CTX boundary.

SSL_CTX_set_srp_username/SSL_CTX_set_srp_password use the same free-then-CRYPTO_strdup order as the pre-fix SSL_set_srp_server_param. CALLER_ALIAS: SSL_CTX_set_srp_username(ctx, SSL_get_srp_username(s)) where the connection's login is NULL hands back the context's own field and the control frees it before duplicating. This is the same B16-D2 class and should be repaired in ssl_lib.rs's ssl3_ctx_ctrl arms.

residuals.description: SSL_set_srp_server_param_pw overwrites srp_ctx.n/g with fresh BN_dup results without releasing the previous values, and srp_server_param_with_username overwrites b/b_pub on repeated calls. The authority does the same; these are leaks, not UB, and changing the overwrite order would alter the allocation-failure state.

ssl_ctx_srp_ctx_init_intern and ssl_srp_ctx_init_intern memset the credential block. Used on a live context/connection through the exported init entry points, this drops any previously owned strings and BIGNUMs without release. The authority's own memset has the same effect; the reset is the documented semantics of those functions.

ssl_srp_ctx_init_intern's failure path calls ssl_srp_ctx_free_intern, which restores strength = SRP_MINIMAL_N; the authority's err arm memsets without restoring strength. The connection is not published on this path (SSL_new fails), so the value is unobservable, but the delta is recorded.

The authority raises ERR_R_BN_LIB/ERR_R_INTERNAL_ERROR when a BN_dup or OPENSSL_strdup fails in ssl_srp_ctx_init_intern. This crate has no generated tls_srp.c sites and raises nothing on those arms. Return values and ownership are unchanged; only the queue contents differ.

residuals.disposition: RETAINED - C callback contract under a read lock
residuals.description: ENGINE_pkey_asn1_find_str invokes the application pkey_asn1_meths callback while holding the global engine read lock, exactly as the authority does. A callback that requests the write lock (for example by registering or removing an engine) would deadlock or fail; the callback contract must remain read-only with respect to the engine table.

ENGINE_get_pkey_asn1_meth_str and engine_pkey_asn1_meths_free call the callback with no crate lock and treat the returned method as engine-owned. The method remains valid only while the engine is alive; the by-name free path and the engine destructor are the authority's own ordering.

int_engine_configure reads the section's CONF_VALUE stack across ENGINE_ctrl_cmd_string/ENGINE_set_default_string/ENGINE_init calls. An application hook that mutates the CONF section being walked would invalidate the iteration; the authority has the same requirement. No crate lock is held, so reentrant configuration loading itself is safe.

residuals.disposition: OUT OF SCOPE - escalated as E2
residuals.description: The context-level username/password controls still free before duplicating. They are in ssl_lib.rs, outside this four-file batch; escalation E2 records the alias case.

If an engine finish hook re-enters configuration loading after the finish walk has observed the stack empty and cleared it, the reentrant engine is recorded on a fresh stack and released by a later finish. The authority's tighter loop may consume it in the same walk; both are safe, and the observable engine lifetime only extends.

graduation: CONTRACTED for all thirteen boundaries. Every remaining unsafe operation has an explicit validity contract and SAFETY comment, every required precondition is established by its callers or by the C ABI contract, and no safe caller can cause UB through the audited interfaces under those contracts. Hidden obligations 0. Not SAFETY_DISCHARGED: full Miri (Stacked/Tree Borrows), Loom/TSan, the authority differentials for B16-D1/D2/D3/D5, independent review and SEAL are NOT_RUN. ASan covered the B16-D2 control only. No SAFE_COMPATIBLE claim.
